name: Regular and Permanent Resident Card

requirements.blocker_text: Law No. 1997/012 on the entry, stay, and exit of foreigners in Cameroon: a foreigner authorized to stay between 2 and 6 consecutive years holds a 2-year renewable resident card ('carte de résidence'). Any resident over 18 must obtain this card within 3 months of entry or face deportation. Required at entry: a valid passport with entry visa, proof of repatriation guarantee, and proof of means of subsistence.
requirements.fix_path: Obtain a resident card within 3 months of entry, maintaining authorized status; renew every 2 years.

requirements.blocker_text: Law No. 1997/012: a foreigner with at least 6 years of uninterrupted residence in Cameroon qualifies for a 10-year renewable permanent resident card, a materially longer validity than the regular resident card.
requirements.fix_path: Maintain 6 years of uninterrupted residence in Cameroon on a regular resident card, then apply for the 10-year permanent card.

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: 6 years uninterrupted residence for the permanent card

STATUS: DRAFT -- the residence-ladder structure is confirmed directly from the primary statute text, hosted on Refworld (tier 2 by this dataset's rules, since it is intergovernmental/UNHCR-hosted primary legal text, not a secondary summary); the validator requires tier-1 (government) sourcing for a hard requirement before a route can be published, and no Cameroonian government source for Law 1997/012 was reached, so this stays draft despite the structural finding itself being solid. GENUINE, CLEAR STRUCTURAL FINDING: unlike Mali, Niger, Haiti, and Bosnia earlier in this dataset (all single/parallel-status systems with no temporary-to-permanent ladder), Cameroon has an explicit, numerically defined two-step residence ladder (2-year card at 2-6 years' stay, 10-year card at 6+ years uninterrupted) directly comparable to Kosovo's ladder found earlier in this session. Dependent children under 18 living with and financially dependent on a cardholding parent automatically receive derivative card status under the same law -- a real, disclosed family provision distinct from the marriage-based route (see cm_family_reunification.json).
